Take \(P(z)=z^2+1\), \(Q(z)=z^3+2\), and \(S(z)=-(z-1)^6\). Then \(S(0)=-1\), and define
\[
R(z)=P(z)Q(z)-S(z)=(z^2+1)(z^3+2)+(z-1)^6.
\]
Then \(P,Q,R\) have the required degrees and constant terms. The equation becomes
\[
P(z)Q(z)-R(z)=-(z-1)^6=0,
\]
whose only distinct root is \(z=1\). Thus \(N=1\) is possible, and since a degree-6 polynomial must have at least one complex root, the minimum is \(1\).

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
